open_points.subject: A11 attempt numbering definition
open_points.text: "An attempt is one execution of a function element, or one send of an operation element..." and later in the same rule: "the pre-send checks of A09 rule 6 — when one fails, an attempt takes the next number and concludes at once"
open_points.question: Does a pre-send failure count as an attempt even though no send happened, or should attempt numbers be reserved only for real sends/executions?
options: Count pre-send failures as attempts (number consumed, NodeExecution written, no EffectAttempt)
Do not count pre-send failures as attempts (no number consumed until a send/execution starts)
open_points.default_guess: Count pre-send failures as attempts, because the later sentence in A11 is more operationally specific.

open_points.subject: A10 refused approval numbering vs A11 numbering invariant
open_points.text: A10 rule 3: "Refusing writes one NodeExecution `refused_by_owner` ... with the next attempt number"; A11 rule 1: "Nothing else takes a number."
open_points.question: Should `refused_by_owner` consume an attempt number even though no execution/send occurred?
options: Yes, refusal consumes the next attempt number
No, refusal is outside attempt numbering and should have no attempt number (or a fixed non-attempt marker)
open_points.default_guess: Yes, consume the next number, because A10 explicitly prescribes it for refusal records.

open_points.subject: Sandbox determinism boundary (A03 vs K-02 no randomness)
open_points.text: K-02 requires "no ... randomness"; A03 lists trapped randomness entry points but closes the list per release (e.g., no statement about interpreter hash seed randomness or other nondeterministic runtime behaviors).
open_points.question: Must the sandbox/runtime also force deterministic interpreter settings (for example fixed hash seed) beyond the explicit trap list?
options: Force deterministic runtime settings (e.g., fixed `PYTHONHASHSEED`) as part of A03
Rely only on the explicit trap list and accept residual nondeterminism if it appears
open_points.default_guess: Force deterministic runtime settings in addition to traps.

open_points.subject: A09 multipart value-part JSON encoding
open_points.text: "a `multipart/form-data` body with one part per other input port ... a value part carrying its JSON"
open_points.question: What exact JSON byte form is sent in multipart value parts (canonical/minified, UTF-8 policy, null handling formatting), and is it required to be stable across runs?
options: Canonical JSON bytes for each value part
Any valid JSON encoding (service-visible but not kernel-constrained)
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical JSON bytes for stability.

open_points.subject: A08 `service_id` lexical rule
open_points.text: "A `service_id` is lowercase letters, digits and `_` only"
open_points.question: Is the empty string a valid `service_id` under this rule, or must at least one character be required?
options: Allow empty string because it contains no disallowed characters
